title: OpenContext carrier flattening + middleware adapter for robust request flow anchoring
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: introduce an SDK middleware adapter that flattens heterogeneous 'context carriers' into a single deterministic header set (OpenContext format), add a lightweight request-flow anchor so background workers and async hops can re-associate with the originating trace, and expose compact span annotations for downstream sampling/aggregation.

Motivation: we see multiple internal + external clients sending different propagation formats (W3C, legacy-x, custom keypairs). This leaks sampling decisions and causes missing child spans on async hops. Current ad-hoc adapters make debugging and dashboard aggregation brittle. Flattening carriers to a canonical OpenContext header allows the runtime + console to reliably surface request lineage and calculate tail-latency per route.

Scope:
- SDK middleware for Node/Python/Go that:
  * normalizes incoming propagation headers into OpenContext (deterministic keys, single envelope header).
  * emits a minimal request-flow-anchor header (openctx-anchor) containing lightweight origin ID + hop counter.
  * preserves original headers in a debug-mode replication header.
- Runtime compatibility layer to accept openctx-anchor in worker replays and queue consumers.
- Console metric mapping: new dashboards for request-flow split-rate, anchor hop count distribution, and anchor-recovery success rate.

Out of scope for this ticket: full OTLP migration of clients, long-term storage format changes, or changing default sampling rates across tenants.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- Single-envelope header reduces header bloat but requires careful base64 length limits (we cap at 2KB). If envelope exceeds limit we fall back to hashed reference stored in a fast lookup (see follow-up ticket).
- We intentionally keep anchor payload minimal (origin-id + 1 byte flags + hop counter) to avoid PII and reduce header size.
- We will implement graceful degradation: if incoming propagation cannot be normalized, we attach an inert openctx-anchor with recovery=false so downstream can surface 'unknown-origin' traces.
- We considered mutating existing headers in-place but chose header-envelope approach to avoid breaking opaque proxies and CDN caches.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK middleware implemented for Node and Python with tests that verify normalization across W3C, B3, and example legacy formats.
- Runtime accepts openctx-anchor and correctly re-associates queued/background work within 95% of synthetic multi-hop requests in canary.
- Console shows new panels for anchor-recovery rate and hop-count distribution; panels updated with synthetic traffic within the canary window.
- No increase in 95th percentile request header size beyond 8KB for a representative workload.
- Feature flag gate present to roll out to 10% / 50% / 100% of traffic per route.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) SDK: create opencontext library that exposes parse(), normalize(), and emit_headers() utilities. Integrate into Node/Python SDK middleware. (week 1)
2) Runtime: add lightweight anchor handler that reads openctx-anchor and maps to request context; if missing, consult debug replication header. (week 2)
3) Console: add metric instrumentation and create dashboards; wire synthetic job to emit test flows. (week 2)
4) Canary: enable feature flag on internal routes -> platform services -> external tenant subset; monitor anchor-recovery and error rates. (week 3)

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for header normalization with fuzz inputs.
- Integration tests: multi-service chain with queue (SQS-like) and worker to verify reattachment of async spans.
- Load test: confirm header parsing path remains <1ms p95 on typical payloads.
- Security review: ensure anchor header contains no user-identifiable data.

Rollout and observability:
- Add rollout toggles in Console with automatic rollback thresholds: anchor-recovery < 85% or error increase > 2x triggers rollback.
- Create lightweight synthetic runner that emits known-origin requests to validate hop counters.
- Add Info-level audit log when an incoming carrier is normalized (debug mode), with sampling to avoid log explosion.

Links and artifacts:

- Runtime PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1890
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/opencontext-dashboard-v1.png
